lesson: Lesson 1: Collaboration with Families and Colleagues

questions.prompt: Match each task to the member of the special education team responsible for the task.
pairs: Offers emotional support and guidance on social issues
Provides specialized instruction and adapts materials to meet student needs
Shares insights about the child’s strengths, needs, and home life
Communicates their goals and preferences for their own education
Delivers content knowledge and supports classroom management

questions.prompt: Mei and Ahmed are co-teaching a classroom that includes students with exceptionalities. Mei is a special education teacher, and Ahmed is a general education teacher. They are planning a lesson and want to ensure that both their expertise is used effectively. What would be the best approach for them to take?
options: Ahmed and Mei should divide the class and teach different lessons simultaneously.
Ahmed should lead the lesson alone, while Mei observes from the back.
Mei should teach the entire lesson while Ahmed gives feedback on papers.
Mei can provide modifications and support during Ahmed’s lesson, making sure that all students can access the content.
questions.note: Source marks option 4 correct; co-teaching also calls for substantive shared planning and responsibility, so do not generalize this answer into a rule that one teacher always leads.

questions.prompt: Jack’s parents are feeling overwhelmed because of his recent diagnosis of a learning disability. As his teacher, you want to empower the family and support Jack's education. What is the most effective first step you can take?
options: Arrange a meeting to discuss Jack’s strengths, needs, and available resources.
Suggest that Jack’s parents attend a support group without school involvement.
Encourage the parents to leave all decisions to the school professionals.
Provide the parents with educational articles without further explanation.
questions.note: Source feedback pasted under this question refers to Mei and co-teaching; preserve reported correctness but flag feedback as misattributed.

questions.prompt: Which three of the following are essential components of effective co-teaching? Select three answers.
options: Mutual planning time to discuss lesson goals and student needs.
Co-teaching should only occur when the principal is present.
Only the special education teacher is responsible for modifying assignments.
Sharing equal responsibility for instruction and assessment.
Maintaining open communication and collaboration between co-teachers.
Each teacher should manage their own students separately.
questions.note: All three source explanations confirm planning, shared instruction/assessment, and open communication.
